title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall-b42 metabolic fork: replicated on fresh seed 4 (every cell dead within ~1500 t of the feed cut; fed twin 28 cells, 14 persistent splits, generation 4), with death a near-instant wall collapse
summary: I looked at fork_s0.png and fork_s1.png, then ran world.py (fed) and world_starve.py (feed cut at t=60000) with labkit on new seed 4 (128^2, 200 frames x 500 steps). The two runs are identical until the cut. In the fed run, walled cells form from noise and divide (persistent splits 14, generation 4, 28 cells at t=100000; fed/seed4/sheet.png). In the starved twin the green wall and blue catalyst of every cell vanish by t=60500, leaving only rings of M wall material, which fade by t=61500; 0 cells remain at the end (fork_s4.png; starve/seed4/FACTS.md: final 0 components). So the cells depend on the consumed, fed substrate, as claimed.

observations.I: fork_s4.png top row: 25-30 discrete walled cells
observations.E: fork_s4.png: every cell gone within ~1500 t of the cut at t=60000; fed twin 28 cells at t=100000

seeds_run.result: pass: fed 28 cells / 14 persistent splits / gen 4; starved 0 cells by t~61500

controls_run.E: starve/seed4 (world_starve.py, feed cut at t=60000) against fed/seed4, identical until the cut

verdicts.limitation: Death is a near-instant collapse: walls and catalyst are gone within ~500 t, so there is no reserve or graded starvation, and the dependence is written into the update (the wall and catalyst are made from S directly). This is E by construction. One fresh seed, global feed cut only (no local cut).
